hardinessNote: Hardy to approximately −20 to −15°C. Suitable throughout the UK in a sheltered position, although emerging foliage can suffer from late spring frosts and cold winds.
visual: A striking, weeping Japanese maple with deeply dissected, lace-like leaves in rich burgundy-purple to dark crimson. Its arching branches create a broad, cascading mound, often becoming more upright with age. The foliage develops brilliant scarlet-red tones in autumn before falling, revealing an elegant branching structure.
pest: Aphids, Acer gall mites, caterpillars and scale insects. Potential diseases include Verticillium wilt and honey fungus.
soil: Fertile, humus-rich, moist but well-drained soil. Prefers slightly acidic to neutral conditions. Suitable for loam, sand and improved clay.
soilWarning: Avoid waterlogged ground, very dry soil, exposed windy sites and strongly alkaline conditions. Delicate leaves can scorch in intense afternoon sunlight, especially during drought. Provide shelter from drying winds and late frosts.
water: Water regularly while establishing, maintaining evenly moist soil without saturation. Provide deep watering during prolonged summer drought. Container specimens require more frequent watering, especially in warm weather.
prune: Minimal pruning required. Remove dead, damaged or crossing branches during dormancy. Avoid heavy pruning and preserve the naturally cascading shape. Minor shaping can be carried out in midsummer to reduce sap bleeding.
